revealWordProblem.title: Apply: The Rooftop Garden
revealWordProblem.text: The firm is designing a regular decagon-shaped rooftop garden bed. It decomposes into 10 congruent triangles from the center, each with a base of 3 feet and a height of 4 feet. The garden center charges $5 per square foot for soil and plants. What is the total cost to fill the garden bed?
revealWordProblem.sampleAnswer: One triangle: A = ½ × 3 × 4 = 6 sq ft. The decagon has 10 sides, so it has 10 triangles: 10 × 6 = 60 sq ft. Cost = 60 × $5 = $300.

conceptIntro.heading: Let's build it together — How do we find the area of a regular polygon?
conceptIntro.intro: A regular polygon is a closed shape with straight sides where every side is the same length and every angle is the same size. We can decompose it (break it apart) into equal triangles from the center, then add up their areas. We'll walk through a worked example, try one together, then you'll try a few with hints right there when you need them.
conceptIntro.keyIdea: A regular polygon splits into the same number of triangles as it has sides, so total area = (one triangle's area) × (number of sides).

iDo.title: Watch me
lines: My hexagon has 6 equal sides. Each side is 6 feet, and each center triangle has a height of 5.2 feet.
First I find one triangle: A = ½ × base × height = ½ × 6 × 5.2.
I multiply: 6 × 5.2 = 31.2, then ½ × 31.2 = 15.6 square feet.
A hexagon has 6 sides, so it has 6 equal triangles.
I multiply: 6 × 15.6 = 93.6. So the total area is 93.6 square feet.

weDo.title: Let's try together
lines: Now a smaller regular pentagon: each of its 5 triangles has base 4 cm and height 3 cm.
First find one triangle: ½ × 4 × 3. What is 4 × 3? Yes, 12, and half of 12 is 6 sq cm.
A pentagon has 5 sides, so how many triangles? Yes, 5.
Multiply: 5 × 6 = 30, so the total area is 30 square centimeters.
Sentence frame — say it with me: "The area of one triangle is ___ , so the whole polygon is ___ ."

explore.instructions: Quick warm-up together: Four design teams each found the area of a regular polygon by decomposing it into congruent triangles. Sort every work sample by what the team actually did.

items.text: Hexagon, side 8 ft, triangle height 7 ft: 6 × (½ × 8 × 7) = 168 sq ft
Pentagon, side 6 ft, triangle height 4 ft: 5 × (½ × 6 × 4) = 60 sq ft
Square, side 10 ft, triangle height 5 ft: 4 × (½ × 10 × 5) = 100 sq ft
Hexagon, side 8 ft, triangle height 7 ft: 6 × (8 × 7) = 336 sq ft
Pentagon, side 6 ft, triangle height 4 ft: 5 × (6 × 4) = 120 sq ft
Hexagon, side 8 ft, triangle height 7 ft: ½ × 8 × 7 = 28 sq ft
Octagon, side 5 ft, triangle height 6 ft: ½ × 5 × 6 = 15 sq ft

explore.label: Sort each team's work: correct, dropped the ½, or stopped after one triangle.
explore.hint: Read the work, not the answer. Ask two questions: did they take HALF of base × height, and did they count EVERY triangle?
hints: Every correct sample has two moves in it — a ½ somewhere, and a multiplication by the number of triangles.
If the ½ is missing, the team measured a rectangle-sized piece instead of a triangle, so their answer is exactly double what it should be.
If there is no multiplication by the triangle count, the team found one slice and called it the whole polygon. Start with the three hexagon cards — same polygon, three different treatments.
explore.explanation: Every regular polygon here follows total area = (number of triangles) × (½ × base × height). The three correct samples do both moves. The 336 and 120 samples multiplied base × height without halving it, so each answer is exactly double the truth (168 and 60). The 28 and 15 samples stopped after one triangle and never multiplied by the 6 or 8 triangles that make up the whole polygon.
explore.explanationEs: Cada polígono regular aquí sigue: área total = (número de triángulos) × (½ × base × altura). Las tres muestras correctas hacen los dos pasos. Las muestras de 336 y 120 multiplicaron base × altura sin sacar la mitad, así que su respuesta es exactamente el doble de la correcta (168 y 60). Las muestras de 28 y 15 se detuvieron en un solo triángulo y nunca multiplicaron por los 6 u 8 triángulos que forman el polígono completo.
explore.instructionsEs: Cuatro equipos de diseño hallaron el área de un polígono regular descomponiéndolo en triángulos congruentes. Clasifica cada muestra de trabajo según lo que el equipo realmente hizo.
hintsEs: Cada muestra correcta tiene dos pasos: un ½ en alguna parte y una multiplicación por el número de triángulos.
Si falta el ½, el equipo midió una pieza del tamaño de un rectángulo en vez de un triángulo, así que su respuesta es exactamente el doble.
Si no hay multiplicación por la cantidad de triángulos, el equipo halló una sola porción y la llamó el polígono entero. Empieza con las tres tarjetas del hexágono.

approaching.stem: A regular hexagon is divided into 6 equal triangles from the center. Each triangle has a base of 6 ft and a height of 5.2 ft. What is the area of one triangle?
approaching.explanation: A = ½ × b × h = ½ × 6 × 5.2 = 15.6 square feet.
choiceFeedback: 31.2 is 6 × 5.2 — the full rectangle. One triangle is half of that: multiply by ½.
11.2 comes from adding 6 + 5.2. Area means multiply base × height, then take half.
The number is right, but ft measures length. Area needs square units (sq ft).
hints: Focus on just ONE of the 6 triangles: its base is 6 ft and its height is 5.2 ft.
One triangle uses A = ½ × b × h — don't multiply by 6 yet; that step is for the whole hexagon.
Compute ½ × 6 × 5.2: take half of 6 first, then multiply by 5.2. Label it in sq ft.
approaching.stemEs: Un hexágono regular se divide en 6 triángulos iguales desde el centro. Cada triángulo tiene una base de 6 ft y una altura de 5.2 ft. ¿Cuál es el área de un triángulo?
approaching.explanationEs: A = ½ × b × h = ½ × 6 × 5.2 = 15.6 pies cuadrados.

approaching.stem: Using the triangle from the previous question, what is the total area of the hexagonal skylight?
approaching.explanation: Total area = 6 triangles × 15.6 sq ft = 93.6 square feet.
choiceFeedback: Is this a rectangle plus a triangle?
Compute each area separately.
Add them.
hints: You already found one triangle's area (15.6 sq ft) in the last question — now think about the whole hexagon.
A regular hexagon splits into 6 identical triangles, so the total is 6 copies of one triangle's area.
Multiply 15.6 × 6. (Tip: do 15 × 6, then 0.6 × 6, and combine.)
approaching.stemEs: Usando el triángulo de la pregunta anterior, ¿cuál es el área total del tragaluz hexagonal?
approaching.explanationEs: Área total = 6 triángulos × 15.6 pies cuadrados = 93.6 pies cuadrados.

approaching.stem: A regular hexagon is split into 6 triangles, each with base 4 cm and height 3.5 cm. What is the total area?
approaching.explanation: Each triangle: ½ × 4 × 3.5 = 7 sq cm. Total: 6 × 7 = 42 sq cm.
choiceFeedback: Identify all simple shapes.
Use the right formula for each.
Sum for the composite area.
hints: Two stages hide here: first one triangle (base 4 cm, height 3.5 cm), then all 6 of them.
Use ½ × 4 × 3.5 for one triangle, then multiply that result by 6 for the hexagon.
Compute ½ × 4 = 2, then 2 × 3.5 for one triangle. Now scale up by the 6 triangles.
approaching.stemEs: Un hexágono regular se divide en 6 triángulos, cada uno con base 4 cm y altura 3.5 cm. ¿Cuál es el área total?
approaching.explanationEs: Cada triángulo: ½ × 4 × 3.5 = 7 cm cuadrados. Total: 6 × 7 = 42 cm cuadrados.

approaching.stem: How many triangles can you make from the center of a regular pentagon?
approaching.explanation: A regular pentagon has 5 sides, so drawing lines from the center to each vertex creates 5 equal triangles.
choiceFeedback: A pentagon has 5 sides — one triangle forms per side.
Count the pentagon's sides again — one triangle each.
Too many — one triangle per side, and a pentagon has 5.
hints: 'Penta' is a clue about how many sides a pentagon has.
Drawing from the center to each corner makes exactly one triangle per side of the polygon.
Count the pentagon's sides — that count equals the number of triangles.
approaching.stemEs: ¿Cuántos triángulos puedes formar desde el centro de un pentágono regular?
approaching.explanationEs: Un pentágono regular tiene 5 lados, así que trazar líneas desde el centro hasta cada vértice crea 5 triángulos iguales.

approaching.title: Spot the Common Mistake

workedExample.label: Find the area of one triangle

approaching.correctWork: An octagon has 8 sides, not 5. Total area = 8 × 6 = 48 sq ft — multiply one triangle's area by the actual number of sides (triangles), not a random number.
hints: Look at Step 4. How many sides does an octagon actually have?
An octagon has 8 sides, so it has 8 triangles: Total = 8 × 6 = 48 sq ft, not 5 × 6.
approaching.explanation: The area of one triangle, 6 sq ft, is right, but the final step multiplied by 5 when an octagon decomposes into 8 triangles. Multiplying by the true number of sides gives Total = 8 × 6 = 48 sq ft.
approaching.explanationEs: El área de un triángulo, 6 pies cuadrados, está bien, pero el último paso multiplicó por 5 cuando un octágono se descompone en 8 triángulos. Al multiplicar por el número real de lados se obtiene un total de 8 × 6 = 48 pies cuadrados.

approaching.stem: A regular hexagonal floor tile splits from its center into 6 congruent triangles, each with an area of 12 cm². What is the total area of the tile?
approaching.explanation: A hexagon has 6 sides, so it splits into 6 equal triangles. Total = 6 × 12 = 72 cm².
choiceFeedback: Identify each simple shape.
Find the area of each.
Add them together for the total.
approaching.stemEs: Una baldosa hexagonal regular se divide desde su centro en 6 triángulos congruentes, cada uno con un área de 12 cm². ¿Cuál es el área total de la baldosa?
approaching.explanationEs: Un hexágono tiene 6 lados, así que se divide en 6 triángulos iguales. Total = 6 × 12 = 72 cm².
hints: A regular polygon splits from its center into one triangle for each side, and all of those triangles are congruent.
Count the sides to know how many triangles there are, then multiply by the area of a single triangle.
A hexagon has 6 sides, so there are 6 triangles worth 12 cm² each. Set up that multiplication and finish it.
hintsEs: Un polígono regular se divide desde su centro en un triángulo por cada lado, y todos esos triángulos son congruentes.
Cuenta los lados para saber cuántos triángulos hay y luego multiplica por el área de un solo triángulo.
Un hexágono tiene 6 lados, así que hay 6 triángulos de 12 cm² cada uno. Plantea esa multiplicación y termínala.

onLevel.stem: A regular pentagonal tile splits into 5 congruent triangles. Each triangle has a base of 4 in and a height of 6 in. What is the total area of the tile?
onLevel.explanation: One triangle = ½ × 4 × 6 = 12 in². A pentagon has 5 triangles, so total = 5 × 12 = 60 in².
choiceFeedback: What shapes do you see? Rectangle? Triangle?
Use the correct formula for each shape.
Sum the areas.
onLevel.stemEs: Una baldosa pentagonal regular se divide en 5 triángulos congruentes. Cada triángulo tiene una base de 4 in y una altura de 6 in. ¿Cuál es el área total de la baldosa?
onLevel.explanationEs: Un triángulo = ½ × 4 × 6 = 12 in². Un pentágono tiene 5 triángulos, así que el total = 5 × 12 = 60 in².
hints: Every regular polygon breaks into congruent triangles, one for each side.
Find the area of one triangle with ½ × base × height, then multiply by the number of triangles.
One triangle is ½ × 4 × 6. Work that out, then multiply your result by the 5 triangles in a pentagon.
hintsEs: Todo polígono regular se descompone en triángulos congruentes, uno por cada lado.
Halla el área de un triángulo con ½ × base × altura y luego multiplica por el número de triángulos.
Un triángulo es ½ × 4 × 6. Calcula eso y luego multiplica tu resultado por los 5 triángulos del pentágono.

onLevel.stem: An octagon tile splits into equal triangles, each with base 6 ft and height 5 ft. How many triangles, and what is the total area?
onLevel.explanation: An octagon has 8 sides, so it splits into 8 triangles. One triangle = ½ × 6 × 5 = 15 sq ft. Total = 8 × 15 = 120 sq ft.
choiceFeedback: That's one triangle — an octagon has 8; multiply.
Check how many triangles an octagon makes — is it 6 or 8?
Recount the triangles (an octagon has 8) and multiply.
onLevel.stemEs: Una baldosa octagonal se divide en triángulos iguales, cada uno con base 6 ft y altura 5 ft. ¿Cuántos triángulos hay y cuál es el área total?
onLevel.explanationEs: Un octágono tiene 8 lados, así que se divide en 8 triángulos. Un triángulo = ½ × 6 × 5 = 15 pies cuadrados. Total = 8 × 15 = 120 pies cuadrados.
hints: An octagon has 8 sides, so it splits from the center into 8 congruent triangles.
Find the area of one triangle first with ½ × base × height, then multiply by the number of triangles.
One triangle is ½ × 6 × 5 = 15 sq ft. Now multiply that by the number of triangles an octagon has.
hintsEs: Un octágono tiene 8 lados, así que se divide desde el centro en 8 triángulos congruentes.
Primero halla el área de un triángulo con ½ × base × altura y luego multiplica por el número de triángulos.
Un triángulo es ½ × 6 × 5 = 15 pies cuadrados. Ahora multiplica eso por el número de triángulos que tiene un octágono.

workedExample.label: Decompose the tile

onLevel.correctWork: The student stopped after finding ONE triangle. A hexagon has 6 congruent triangles, so multiply by 6: Total = 6 × 14 = 84 sq in.

onLevel.titleEs: Extensión de Nivel 2 — encuentra el error del área de la baldosa
onLevel.explanation: The final step reported 14 sq in, which is only ONE of the hexagon's six congruent triangles. Multiplying by the triangle count finishes the job: Total = 6 × 14 = 84 sq in.
onLevel.explanationEs: El paso final informó 14 pulgadas cuadradas, que es solo UNO de los seis triángulos congruentes del hexágono. Multiplicar por la cantidad de triángulos completa el trabajo: total = 6 × 14 = 84 pulgadas cuadradas.

onLevel.title: Find the Area Error
onLevel.correctWork: To find total area, multiply (not add): Total = 10.75 × 6 = 64.5 sq m. Six equal triangles means 6 times one triangle's area.
hints: Look at Step 4. What operation should you use to combine 6 equal triangles?
The student added 10.75 + 6 instead of multiplying 10.75 × 6.
onLevel.explanation: One triangle at 10.75 sq m is correct, but the last step added the 6 instead of using it as a count. Six congruent triangles means six copies of that area, so Total = 10.75 × 6 = 64.5 sq m.
onLevel.explanationEs: Un triángulo de 10.75 metros cuadrados está bien, pero el último paso sumó el 6 en lugar de usarlo como cantidad. Seis triángulos congruentes significan seis copias de esa área, así que el total es 10.75 × 6 = 64.5 metros cuadrados.

onLevel.prompt: A regular hexagon and a regular pentagon both have triangles with the same base (6 ft) and the same height (5 ft). Which polygon has the greater total area? Explain why the number of sides matters.
onLevel.sentenceFrame: One triangle's area is ½ × ___ × ___ = ___. The hexagon has ___ triangles so its area is ___. The pentagon has ___ triangles so its area is ___. The ___ has more area because ___.
onLevel.hint: Identify each shape; write area formula; add results.
hints: Both polygons use identical triangles (base 6 ft, height 5 ft) — only the NUMBER of triangles differs.
Find one triangle's area with ½ × 6 × 5, then multiply by 6 for the hexagon and by 5 for the pentagon.
Compute ½ × 6 × 5 for one triangle. Then compare 6 copies with 5 copies and explain why the counts matter.
onLevel.explanation: One triangle is ½ × 6 × 5 = 15 sq ft in both polygons, so the only difference is how many copies each shape holds: the hexagon has 6 for 90 sq ft and the pentagon has 5 for 75 sq ft. The hexagon has the greater area because the number of sides is exactly the number of identical triangles you get to add.
onLevel.explanationEs: Un triángulo mide ½ × 6 × 5 = 15 pies cuadrados en los dos polígonos, así que la única diferencia es cuántas copias tiene cada figura: el hexágono tiene 6 para 90 pies cuadrados y el pentágono tiene 5 para 75. El hexágono tiene mayor área porque el número de lados es exactamente la cantidad de triángulos iguales que puedes sumar.

onLevel.instructions: Sort each polygon by whether it decomposes into more than 5 triangles or 5 or fewer.
onLevel.hint: For each figure, break it into simpler shapes and add areas.
hints: Each card already tells you the triangle count after the arrow — compare that number to 5.
'More than 5' is strictly greater; a polygon with exactly 5 triangles belongs in '5 or fewer'.
First card: a hexagon makes 6 triangles. Is 6 more than 5? Place it, then repeat with each polygon.
onLevel.explanation: A regular polygon splits into one triangle per side, so the triangle count matches the number of sides. The hexagon (6) and the octagon (8) are the only cards above 5, while the equilateral triangle (3), the square (4), and the pentagon (exactly 5) all belong in the '5 or fewer' group.
onLevel.explanationEs: Un polígono regular se divide en un triángulo por cada lado, así que la cantidad de triángulos coincide con el número de lados. El hexágono (6) y el octágono (8) son las únicas tarjetas por encima de 5, mientras que el triángulo equilátero (3), el cuadrado (4) y el pentágono (exactamente 5) van en el grupo de '5 o menos'.

practice.commonMistake: A common mistake in Area of Regular Polygons is stopping after finding the area of ONE triangle and reporting that as the total area — or adding the number of triangles instead of multiplying. Remember: total area = (one triangle's area) × (number of sides), not (one triangle's area) + (number of sides).

connect.scenario: A city planner is building a regular octagonal gazebo in a park. Each of the 8 triangles formed from the center has a base of 5 feet and a height of 6 feet. The flooring costs $3 per square foot.
connect.promptQuestion: How much will the gazebo flooring cost?
connect.prompt: One triangle's area is ___ sq ft. The octagon has ___ triangles, so total area = ___ sq ft. The cost is ___ x $3 = $___.

check.stem: What is the area of one center triangle?
check.explanation: A = ½ × base × height = ½ × 5 × 6 = 15 sq ft.

check.stem: What is the total floor area of the octagon?
check.explanation: The octagon is made of 8 identical triangles: 8 × 15 = 120 sq ft.

connect.modelAnswer: Each of the 8 center triangles has area ½ × 5 × 6 = 15 sq ft, so the octagon covers 8 × 15 = 120 sq ft. At $3 per square foot the flooring costs 120 × $3 = $360.

exitTicket.stem: Quick check — you've got this: A regular pentagon is decomposed into 5 triangles from its center. Each triangle has a base of 7 inches and a height of 4.8 inches. What is the total area of the pentagon?
exitTicket.explanation: One triangle: A = 1/2 x 7 x 4.8 = 16.8 sq in. Total = 5 x 16.8 = 84 square inches.
choiceFeedback: That's one triangle — multiply by all 5 triangles.
You skipped the ½ — each triangle is ½ × 7 × 4.8.
Right value, wrong unit — area is square inches.
hints: Two steps hide in this problem: one triangle's area first, then all 5 triangles together.
One triangle is ½ × 7 × 4.8; the pentagon is 5 of those. Skipping either step leads to a wrong path.
Take half of 7 × 4.8 to get one triangle's area, then multiply that by the 5 triangles.

parallelPractice.stem: A regular hexagon splits into 6 triangles with base 5 and height 3. Find its area.

Use the visual model, then complete one step at a time.
Start like this: Area of one triangle: 7.5.
parallelPractice.explanation: Area of one triangle: 7.5. Multiply by 6 triangles: 45.

questions.stem: Why do we divide by 2 when finding the area of a triangle?
choices: A triangle is exactly half of a rectangle with the same base and height
The base is always twice the height
We always divide area formulas by 2
questions.explanation: A triangle with base b and height h fits inside a rectangle with the same base and height. The triangle covers exactly half the rectangle, so A = ½ × b × h.

questions.stem: A triangle has an area of 24 sq ft and a base of 8 ft. What is the height?
What is the area of a triangle with base 10 cm and height 6 cm?
questions.explanation: A = ½ × b × h = ½ × 10 × 6 = 30 square centimeters.
